title: Best Office Chairs UK
short: Office chairs compared for comfort, adjustability and build quality, tested through full working days, from budget ergonomic picks to design-icon premium models.
intro: An office chair's real test is how it feels after sitting in it for a full working day, not how it looks in a product shot. This guide compares chairs tested by Expert Reviews, who assembled, sat in and scored each one on comfort, features and ease of use from their London office.

products.name: Task One
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong ergonomics at a reasonable price
products.key_spec: Adjustable seat depth, 4-position recline lock, height/depth/angle-adjustable arms, adjustable lumbar support
products.summary: Expert Reviews' favourite office chair, striking a rare balance of being genuinely comfortable and supportive while looking smart, at a reasonable price for an ergonomic chair. The fabric-upholstered foam seat and mesh backrest stayed comfortable through a full working day, though the armrests are harder than some rivals and forward tilt costs an extra £39.
pros: Comfortable with genuinely supportive features
Smart, unobtrusive design
Strong value for an ergonomic chair
Adjustable lumbar support, seat depth and arms

products.name: M57
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong ergonomics without paying premium prices
products.key_spec: Mesh seat and back, back tilt, adjustable lumbar support, fully adjustable arms, headrest included
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this offers ergonomics and adjustability rarely seen at this price, including a headrest that's uncommon in this bracket. It's the chair Expert Reviews' own Managing Editor uses at home, with a comfortable, cool mesh design and full adjustability, though the reviewer noted it's something of a dust magnet.
pros: Excellent range of ergonomic features for the price
Comfortable, breathable mesh design
Includes a headrest, unusual at this price
Often available discounted during sales

products.name: Aeron
products.best_for: Buyers with the budget for a design-icon chair with class-leading adjustability
products.key_spec: Breathable mesh seat and backrest, extensive adjustability, 159kg max load, MoMA design collection piece
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the breathable, buoyant mesh fabric and plentiful adjustable features made this comfortable and supportive despite lacking cushioning. It's both a pop culture and design icon, with genuinely little to criticise about the chair itself, though at over £1,000 it's only realistic for the biggest budgets.
pros: Exceptional range of adjustable features
Iconic, timeless design
Breathable mesh stays comfortable all day
Little to criticise on comfort or support

products.name: Do Better
products.best_for: Buyers who want automatic adjustment without fiddling with knobs
products.key_spec: Automatic weight-balancing tilt mechanism, adjustable seat depth and lumbar support, 150kg max load
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the standout feature here is a 'weight balancing mechanism' that automatically adjusts tilt tension to the user's weight, hitting a sweet spot without manual fiddling. It's also made from mostly recycled or recyclable materials with a smaller carbon footprint than its predecessor, though the armrests only adjust in height.
pros: Automatic tilt tension removes manual adjustment
Comfortable and supportive
Sustainable materials and lower carbon footprint
Easily adjustable seat depth and lumbar support
cons: Armrest adjustability limited to height only

products.name: Sayl
products.best_for: Buyers who want a genuinely distinctive-looking chair that's still comfortable
products.key_spec: Golden Gate Bridge-inspired unframed backrest, adjustable seat depth, 159kg max load
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this striking chair, inspired by San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge, more comfortable than its hard, rubbery-looking backrest suggests, feeling supportive throughout a working day. It stands out in a world of drab mesh office chairs, though adjustable lumbar support and fully adjustable arms cost extra on top of the standard price.
pros: Genuinely distinctive, striking design
More comfortable and supportive than it looks
Well-built with a design pedigree
Standard version comfortable for a full working day
cons: Adjustable lumbar support and arms cost extra

products.name: Doro S300
products.best_for: Buyers who want maximum adjustability and don't mind paying for it
products.key_spec: Height/depth/width/angle-adjustable arms, 3-position tilt limiter, dual wing-like lumbar support, 136kg max load
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this aerospace-inspired chair adjustable 'to the nth degree', with the most versatile arms tested, adjustable by height, depth, width and angle. The dual wing-like lumbar support proved much more comfortable and supportive than expected, though build quality felt slightly loose in areas and it's expensive at RRP (often discounted in sales).
pros: Extremely extensive adjustability, especially the arms
Excellent, comfortable lumbar support
Heavy, substantial build
Often available for less than RRP
cons: Build quality feels slightly loose in places

guide.q: Does a good office chair really have to cost a lot?
guide.a: Expert Reviews' testing found pricier chairs generally give superior ergonomics, more adjustability and longer warranties, and genuinely cheap two-figure chairs tend to be a false economy in comfort and durability. That said, the budget-priced Sihoo M57 here proves a mid-range chair can offer excellent ergonomics without needing four figures.

guide.q: What adjustments should I prioritise when setting up a new chair?
guide.a: Adjust height, back position and tilt so your lower back feels supported with a slight arch, your knees sit just below your hips, and your feet are flat on the floor or a footrest. Also check the seat depth: when you recline, the backrest shouldn't drop away from your back, and armrests should let your wrists and forearms extend straight out in front of you.

guide.q: How important is a free-float tilt mechanism?
guide.a: Very, according to Expert Reviews' buying advice: the best chairs let you keep moving while seated rather than locking into one static position, since constant subtle movement is healthier for your back than rigid stillness. Features like the Orangebox Do Better's automatic weight-balancing tilt make this easier to get right without manual fiddling.

guide.q: What warranty length should I look for?
guide.a: Expert Reviews recommends a warranty of five years or more for an office chair, since it needs to withstand years of daily use. A long warranty is also often a useful proxy for how confident the manufacturer is in the chair's build quality and longevity.
